1. Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
2. Application stands disposed of.

3. The instant petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Cr.P.C ) has been filed by petitioners praying for quashing of FIR bearing no. 201/2021, registered at Police Station Jyoti Nagar, North East, Delhi for the offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom.

entities.text: Police Station Jyoti Nagar, North East
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 4. Issue notice.
Mr. Naresh Kumar Chahar, learned APP accepts notice on behalf of the State.

5. All the petitioners are present before this Court and have been identified by their counsel Mr.
Manish Sharma and Investigating Officer (IO) SI Sanjay Yadav, Police Station Jyoti Nagar, North East, Delhi.

entities.text: Police Station Jyoti Nagar, North East
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 6. Brief facts of the present case are that marriage of petitioner no.1 and respondent no.2 had been solemnised on 22.04.2015 according to Hindu rites and ceremonies at Delhi and out of this wedlock one female child was born on 13.01.2016.

It is stated that due to temperamental differences and Hom Dutt Sharma And Ors vs The State & Anr. & Ors on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76738385/
1 incapability, serious differences had arisen between petitioner no.1 and respondent no. 2 which resulted into their separation since 30.06.2020 and respondent no.2 had started residing at her parental home.

entities.text: Hom Dutt Sharma And Ors vs The State & Anr. & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The respondent no. 2 lodged a complaint with CAW Cell, Nand Nagari, Delhi against petitioner no. 1 to 4 which culminated into FIR bearing no. 201/2021, registered at Police Station Jyoti Nagar, Delhi, for the offences punishable under Section s 406/498A/34 of IPC.

It is further stated that complainant/respondent no. 2 and the petitioner no. 1 entered into a settlement before Mediation Centre, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi on 29.03.2022.
7.

On a query made by this Court, respondent no.2 who has been identified by the IO, has categorically stated that she has entered into compromise out of her own free will and without any pressure, coercion or threat.
It is also stated by respondent no. 2 that the entire dispute has been amicably settled/compromised between them and they have been living together since 14.04.2022 along with the minor child.
Respondent no. 2 further stated that she has no objection if FIR may be quashed.

8. In view of the above facts that the parties have amicably resolved their differences out of their own free will, and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings, rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
It would thus be in interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
There is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.

9. Accordingly, FIR bearing no. 201/2021, registered at Police Station Jyoti Nagar, North East, Delhi for the offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34of the IPC and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.

entities.text: Police Station Jyoti Nagar, North East, Delhi
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 10. The present petition stands disposed of.
11. The order be uploaded on the website forthwith.
SWARANA KANTA SHARMA, J MARCH 21, 2023/
